audit.why: Ratings must be inverse across the mirror; 7.5/10 on Karma's page is 2.5/10 on Ryze's.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart gave 'Skill' at Level 3 and Level 6 in both layers; the packet chart says Ryze at both, and the mirror kept a Lvl 6 Ryze flip.
audit.why: Level 3 is where Spell Flux makes Rune Prison a root, and Level 6 is Realm Warp against a champion with no dash.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly calls Mantra-Q ('RQ') a tether/root and refers to a Ryze 'W-shield'. Karma's root is Focused Resolve (W); Mantra Q is a delayed cataclysm with a slow. Ryze's W has no shield. It also treats Rune Prison as an unconditional root.
audit.why: Riot text: Inner Flame is a 950-range projectile that explodes, Mantra adding a delayed cataclysm; Focused Resolve is a 675-range tether that roots only if unbroken (flat 12s). Rune Prison slows and roots ONLY through Spell Flux.
audit.corrected: State Rune Prison roots only with Flux applied, that Overload (5s base) resets off W and E casts, that Focused Resolve is broken with distance/line of sight off a flat 12s cooldown, and that Inspire (10/9.5/9/8.5/8s) shields one ally only.

audit.whatIsWrong: No concrete cooldown numbers anywhere; advice says 'when her RQ is on cooldown'.
audit.why: Focused Resolve 12s flat and Inspire 10s at rank 1 are the punish windows.
audit.corrected: Folded the 12s W and 10s Inspire numbers into mid and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal note despite Mantra-W healing Karma on the tether.
audit.why: missingInteractions flags Grievous Wounds timing for extended trades.

edits.before: Even matchup — difficulty 5.5/10, Karma carry threat 6/10.
edits.after: Favoured lane — difficulty 2.5/10, Karma carry threat 6/10.

edits.before: Even matchup — difficulty 5.5/10, Karma carry threat 6/10.
edits.after: Favoured lane — difficulty 2.5/10, Karma carry threat 6/10.

edits.before: You gain W's root and she has to respect the threat of a locked-down empowered Q, making trades genuinely even for the first time.
edits.after: Rune Prison only slows until Spell Flux lands, so level 2 is slow-plus-Overload; real roots wait for E, and Focused Resolve is 12s down.

edits.before: Your full E-Q-W Flux cascade cycles inside her root window and she has no dash to escape; one complete combo drops her to half health.
edits.after: Spell Flux first — then Rune Prison roots instead of slowing and Overload resets off both casts. No dash, so one full chain takes half her health.

edits.before: Karma's RQ tether roots you at range before you can walk into Flux distance — respect the empowered Q poke and don't let her stack early leads.
edits.after: Mantra needs no skill point, so her empowered Inner Flame drops a delayed cataclysm from 950 at level 1 — eat it on the wave, never standing still.

edits.before: Level 3 is your first real window: E onto her to start the Flux mark, then W-root so empowered Q cascades through the bounce and hits her twice while she is locked in place. Her RQ tether requires a channel she cannot complete inside a root, so the single biggest mistake you can make mid-lane is walking into RQ range BEFORE casting W — always root first, then commit. Levels 4-5 are a skill-check grind: her shield and move-speed let her reset trades and you are mana-hungry pre-item, so you hold the combo for when her RQ is visibly on cooldown. At 6 your Realm Warp grants roam and flank threat she cannot E-shield away from for your jungler; she has no answer to a warp-gank coming from behind her.
edits.after: Level 3 is your first real window: Spell Flux onto her, then Rune Prison — with Flux applied it roots instead of slowing — and Overload resets off both casts for a second hit while she is stuck. Focused Resolve only roots if its tether survives, so break it with distance or line of sight instead of standing inside her 675 range. Levels 4-5 are a skill-check grind: Inspire's shield and move speed let her reset trades and you are mana-hungry pre-item, so hold the combo for when her 10-second Inspire and flat 12-second W are both spent. At 6 Realm Warp gives your jungler a flank she cannot shield anyone out of; she has no answer to a gank arriving behind her.

edits.before: First item Seraph's is when this lane stops feeling close — your cooldowns collapse and the Flux-root-empowered Q cycle becomes relentless, putting out sustained magic damage she cannot fully absorb with one shield per trade rotation. At two items you are a teamfight carry whose Flux cascades hit multiple targets Karma's E can only protect one at a time; use Realm Warp to place your team past her peel line and let the AoE loop do the rest. She will try to RQ-root you at the edge of her range before you walk into Flux distance — burn her RQ into your W-shield if you have one up, then punish the full cooldown window.
edits.after: First item Seraph's is when this lane stops feeling close — your cooldowns collapse and the Flux-into-Rune-Prison cycle becomes relentless, putting out sustained magic damage she cannot absorb with one Inspire shield per rotation. At two items you are a teamfight carry whose Flux cascades hit multiple targets Karma's E can only protect one at a time; use Realm Warp to place your team past her peel line and let the loop do the rest. Her lockdown is Focused Resolve, a 675-range tether on a flat 12 seconds that roots only if it is never broken — walk out of it or break sight, then punish the whole twelve.

notes: Mirror (karma__ryze) rates the lane HARD 7.5/10 from Karma's side off a 34.48% win rate on only 29 games; this side has 796 games at 53.52%, which is favoured but not 2.5/10-easy. I followed the mirror to avoid a contradiction — see questionsForUser. The page's biggest error was calling Mantra-Q a root tether: Karma's root is Focused Resolve (W). It also invented a Ryze 'W-shield'. Mantra-W heals Karma on the tether, so Grievous Wounds matters in extended trades; no writable path had room for it inside the length band.
